marks.gloss_en: Zichronot and Shofarot are said only on Rosh HaShana, in Jubilee years and in time of war
the men of the priestly watch and the men of the maamad are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder
מפני מה אמרו ... שמא תכבד העבודה על אנשי בית אב ויבואו ויסייעו להם
why did they say the men of the watch may drink wine at night but not by day? lest the service grow heavy on the men of the beit av, and they come and help them
מפני מה אמרו ... מפני שהן עסוקין תמיד בעבודה
why did they say the men of the beit av neither by day nor by night? because they are constantly engaged in the service
מכאן אמרו -- drawn from the reasons just given
מכאן אמרו (continued)
from here they said: any priest who knows his watch and the watch of his beit av, and knows that his fathers' houses are established there, is forbidden to drink wine that whole day
מכאן אמרו (continued)
one who knows neither his watch nor his beit av's, and knows his fathers' houses are established there, is forbidden to drink wine the whole year
Rebbi: I say -- [by right] it is forbidden [for him] to drink wine ever
בשלמא גבי שמואל -- כתיב ביה תפלה: for Samuel the exchangers' 'Who hears prayer' fits
וכתיב ביה צעקה: for Samuel the mishnah's 'Who hears the cry' fits too
some exchange: 'cry' for Elijah
בשלמא גבי שמואל — כתיב ביה תפלה וכתיב ביה צעקה: granted for Samuel, of whom prayer is written (and crying too)
אתיא פרע פרע מנזיר: here 'and locks [pera] they shall not let grow long' (Ezek 44:20), there 'he shall let the locks [pera] of the hair of his head grow' (Num 6:5); as there thirty, so here thirty
Rav Pappa to Abaye: ודלמא הכי קאמר רחמנא: לא לירבו כלל -- perhaps the verse means [priests] should not grow [their hair] at all, so nothing of thirty days follows
had it said לא ישלחו פרע, as you say; it says ופרע לא ישלחו -- let there be locks, only not grown long (= p_abaye_pera_leihevei)
Rav Matna: unspecified naziriteship is thirty days
אי הכי, אפילו האידנא נמי! -- if so, [priests should cut their hair every thirty days] even nowadays
דומיא דשתויי יין: מה שתויי יין בזמן ביאה הוא דאסור, שלא בזמן ביאה שרי -- אף הכא נמי (= p_dumya_shtuyei_yayin, p_shtuyei_yayin_bizman_bia, p_pruei_rosh_bizman_bia)
[the long-haired are] like those who have drunk wine
והתניא, רבי אומר: כהנים אסורים לשתות יין לעולם... ואמר אביי: כמאן שתו האידנא כהני חמרא -- כרבי; מכלל דרבנן אסרי! -- the Rabbis forbid wine even nowadays, not only at the time of entry
Rebbi: I say priests are forbidden to drink wine forever, but what can I do, for his remedy is his ruin
a king cuts his hair every day
אלא גבי אליהו — תפלה כתיב, צעקה לא כתיב! -- of Elijah only prayer is written, not crying; how can his blessing close with 'Who hears cries'?
״עננו ה׳ עננו״ לשון צעקה היא -- Elijah's 'answer me, Lord, answer me' is itself crying (= p_aneini_lashon_tzeaka)
but of Elijah 'prayer' is written
the mishnah: for the sixth he says 'He Who answered Jonah', for the seventh 'He Who answered David' -- Jonah comes before David
